subject: High-burst guarantees and model-mix pricing — HelioSec Dedicated proposal
messages:
From: Ellie Perez <ellie.perez@heliosec.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliosec.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + Dedicated capacity questions

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement looped me in; we want to understand whether Redwood can commit to a high-burst guarantee for peak events and how that interacts with pricing. A few specifics from our side: 
- Baseline steady traffic ~30 requests/sec (chat-style completions, avg 350 tokens generated).
- Two big monthly flash events (marketing pushes) where we need ~700 concurrent sessions for 10–15 minutes each, peak throughput ~180 req/sec for short windows.
- Model mix: mostly Llama-2-13B for quality, with Mistral-7B for lower-cost user segments (~25% of traffic).
- Average context length: 8k tokens, but 10–15% of requests hit 32k context.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime and latency p95 < 450ms for standard traffic; for burst windows we need a guaranteed failover to higher-capacity pool or documented throttling policy.

Can you share a recommended GPU pool to cover both steady usage and those bursts, and how reserved commits vs burst credits would be priced? Also: can we apply a committed-discount schedule if we sign a 12–24 month reserved commit?

Thanks,
Ellie
Ellie Perez
Head of Product Operations, HelioSec

Hi Ellie — appreciated the details. Quick read and answers up front, then we can sync on numbers.

Summary answers:
- Yes, we can support short, high-intensity bursts with a hybrid approach: a baseline reserved GPU pool sized for steady traffic plus a burst credit bucket (pre-allocated vGPU-hours) that can be consumed for short windows.
- For 32k context requests we recommend reserved nodes with high-memory GPUs (A100 80GB or equivalent) for a portion of the pool; smaller models can run on cheaper 48GB/60GB instances for cost-efficiency.
- Committed discounts scale with the length and size of the commit. 12-month 100% commit yields X% discount; 24-month larger commits increase that discount.

I asked Aditya and Vivek to model throughput & a concrete GPU-pool recommendation based on your profile — will attach a workbook with scenarios. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the pricing table?

Best,
Kimberly

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ellie Perez <ellie.perez@heliosec.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High-burst guarantees and model-mix pricing — sizing scenarios

Ellie / Kimberly — I ran three scenarios and included the workbook proposed-gpu-pool-pricing.xlsx with line-item math. Highlights below (numbers are conservative — factor +10% headroom for safety):

Scenario A — Steady + modest bursts (lower commit)
- Baseline sizing: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes dedicated to Llama-2-13B capacity to handle 30 req/s steady with 8k context (KV cache optimization enabled).
- Secondary pool: 3 x 48GB GPUs for Mistral-7B (25% traffic).
- Burst mechanism: 200 vGPU-hours/month credit bucket (consumable in any pattern). Supports ~150–200 req/s sustained for 10–15 minutes across the pool.
- Expected p95 latency: 280–420ms (depending on sequence length).
- Pricing: modest reserved commit with 6–8% discount vs on-demand.

Scenario B — Higher-reserve + small burst headroom (recommended midpoint)
- Baseline sizing: 12 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (mix of high-memory and general-purpose instances). This provides headroom for longer 32k context at lower p95 penalty.
- Secondary pool: 4 x 48–60GB GPUs for Mistral/aux models.
- Burst credits: 600 vGPU-hours/month. This is sized to absorb two 15-minute flashes at ~180 req/s without failing over to an external region.
- Expected p95 latency: 240–380ms in normal traffic; 360–520ms under peak flash (but with prioritized routing to reserved high-memory nodes for 32k requests).
- Pricing: 12-month commit recommended; discounts 14–18% tier depending on total commit (sheet shows breakpoints).

Scenario C — Heavy-reserve and SLA-backed guarantee
- Baseline sizing: 18 x A100-80GB nodes + 6 x 60–80GB for model-mix.
- Burst mechanism: no separate credits required; pool sized to absorb expected peaks with minimal throttling.
- SLA: explicit latency SLOs for standard traffic and documented runbook for flash events (auto-burst and preemption policies).
- Pricing: 24-month commit, deepest discounts (22–28%).

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Model-mix routing is important: route high-cost Llama traffic to high-memory nodes, autoscale Mistral to cheaper vGPUs.
- We recommend using Redwood Optimize to reduce per-token cost via dynamic quantization on Mistral paths.
- For your 32k context cases (10–15% of traffic) we reserve 20% of high-memory nodes to avoid KV cache thrash.

Next steps proposed:
1) Decide on desired burst tolerance (A/B/C).
2) If B or C, sign an NDA + 12/24-month LOI to lock pricing.
3) We’ll provision a temporary pilot pool with monitoring and run a synthetic flash test (we can simulate your marketing push).

I attached the workbook with per-node compute-hour math and example monthly invoice lines. Happy to jump on a call and walk numbers — Kimberly, can you propose two times?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-gpu-pool-pricing.xlsx (pricing workbook)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-24T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Final recommendation & next steps — HelioSec Dedicated sizing (recommended: Scenario B)

Ellie — thanks for the quick review of Aditya's scenarios. After internal discussion with Vivek (platform) and Aditya (SRE/sizing), we recommend you proceed with Scenario B as the best balance of cost and burst protection. Key deliverables and asks below: 

Recommendation (Scenario B) summary:
- GPU pool: 12 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (mix) + 4 x 48–60GB for lighter models.
- Burst credits: 600 vGPU-hours/month allocated to your account; auto-apply when baseline is saturated.
- 32k handling: reserve ~20% of high-memory nodes for 32k contexts to keep p95 predictable.
- Monitoring: Redwood Console access, custom dashboards for HelioSec, alerting for burst consumption and p95 regressions.
- Pilot: 30-day pilot with live synthetic flash test (we'll coordinate a 15-minute run at 180 req/s).

Pricing & discounts (summary lines — see workbook):
- 12-month reserved commit at the pool sizing above, starting at a 16% discount vs on-demand; pricing improves if committed spend increases or a 24-month term is chosen.
- One-time pilot credit: we can offer a $7,500 pilot credit to cover synthetic tests and initial tuning.
- Commit flexibility: up to 15% monthly bursting beyond the pool covered by burst credits; larger bursts will incur a defined overage rate (sheet lines 18–21).

Next steps:
1) Sign LOI for 12-month reserve (we can add 24-month option in the same DocuSign).
2) We’ll schedule the pilot flash test (Aditya/SRE will run).
3) Procurement: please review the terms in the Drive folder; we can support a standard enterprise amendment for audit/SOC-2 items.

If that sounds good, Ellie — can you confirm by end of week? Kimberly will loop legal for the LOI and Vivek will scope the pilot runbook.

Thanks again — look forward to getting this into pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0123
